ImageDescription.value:
The Washington Post | John Philip Sousa
During the 1880s, the Washington Post sponsored an essay contest for school children known as the Washington Post Amateur Authors’ Association. The owners of the newspaper, Frank Hatton and Beriah Wilkins, asked John Philip Sousa, then leader of the "The President's Own" United States Marine Band, to compose a march for the award ceremony. The march became known as "The Washington Post" march.

Credit.value: YouTube: Anchors Aweigh by 215th Army Band's "Liberty Winds" – View/save archived versions on archive.org

ImageDescription.value:
The 215th Army Band is based in Fall River, MA. Liberty Winds is a wind ensemble consisting of Flute, Oboe, Clarinet, French Horn, and Baritone Saxophone. They are one of several Music Performance Teams that make up our Army Band. Recorded live on October 17, 2021 in our rehearsal room, they are performing the song of the US Navy, Anchors Aweigh.

Follow us for more online:

  • https://www.215tharmyband.com
  • https://www.facebook.com/215thArmyBand/
  • https://www.instagram.com/215tharmyband/
